title: Six-functor datum, axiomatized
statement:
Fix the global finite-field datum
$(p,a,q,k_0,k)$ [def-weil-finite-field-fiber] with $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, a prime $\ell\ne p$, a
finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$ with valuation ring $\mathcal O_E$ and
uniformizer $\varpi_E$, an integer $n\ge1$, and put
$A_{E,n}=\mathcal O_E/\varpi_E^n$ and
$\Lambda\in\{A_{E,n},\mathcal O_E,E,\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell\}$. A *six-functor
datum* is the datum of the
operation datum of [def-fix-six-functor-datum] —
the categories $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ [def-weil-finite-tor-amplitude], the functors $Lf^*,Rf_*,Rf_!, Rf^!$, $-\otimes^L_\Lambda-$, $R\mathcal H om_\Lambda(-,-)$, the
exchange and projection
transformations, the compact-support
direct image $Rf_!=R\bar f_*j_!$ for a compactification, and the
exceptional inverse image
— subject to the following axioms. The coefficient categories, completed integral operations, rationalization, common-stage scalar extension, and dualizing objects are those specified in [def-fix-six-functor-datum]. Schemes and morphisms have its finite-type $k$-scheme setting; each axiom is imposed on the displayed finite-Tor domains, for all composable separated finite-type morphisms. The words separated and proper have the meanings of [def-weil-proper-morphism], and smooth has the meaning of [def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. In (A2) the Cartesian square [def-weil-pbc-cartesian-square] is
$$
\begin{array}{ccc}
X'&\xrightarrow{g'}&X\\
f'\downarrow&&\downarrow f\\
Y'&\xrightarrow{g}&Y.
\end{array}
$$

1. **(A1)** $Lf^*\dashv Rf_*$ and $Rf_!\dashv Rf^!$, with the
pasted units and counits for composites;
1. **(A2)** base change: $Lg^*Rf_!\cong Rf'_!Lg'^*$ for every
Cartesian square, and $Lg^*Rf_*\cong Rf'_*Lg'^*$ for proper $f$ or smooth
$g$;
1. **(A3)** the supplied projection transformation of [def-exchange-projection], of type
$$
\operatorname{PF}_{f,K,L}:Rf_!K\otimes^L_\Lambda L\longrightarrow
Rf_!(K\otimes^L_\Lambda Lf^*L),
$$
is an isomorphism for $K\in D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$ and $L\in D^b_{ctf}(Y,\Lambda)$;
1. **(A4)** the composition law $R(g\circ f)_!\cong Rg_!Rf_!$
with its pentagon, and $Rf_!\cong Rf_*$ for proper $f$;
1. **(A5)** compatibility of all of the above with finite
reduction, scalar extension, and the pro-étale realization, using the coefficient comparison data of [def-exchange-projection] at the stages where those comparisons are defined (finite reduction at finite and integral coefficients, and rationalization and common-stage scalar extension at field coefficients);
1. **(A6)** the dualizing functor
$D_X=R\mathcal H om_X(-,\omega_X)$ is a contravariant exact anti-equivalence
of $D^b_{ctf}(X,\Lambda)$, exact in the sense of [def-weil-triangulated-category] on the opposite triangulated category, with $K\to D_XD_XK$ an isomorphism (Verdier
biduality).

This is an axiomatized framework: a formal consequence may use only the clauses explicitly invoked in its proof. These clauses are required structure and properties, not assertions proved by this definition. For the concrete coefficient system, each clause needs its own verification on the stated domain. The references [thm-weil-six-operations] and [def-sf-pf] are forward pointers to the concrete package and its notation, respectively; they are not prerequisites for this definition.
